clue.text: Top stated means of getting mobile after a fall

definitions.text: means of getting mobile after a fall

indicators.note: something stated is spoken, so the word we want is one that is said the same way as another

parts.note: to top someone is slang for killing them, which is to slay

explanation.surface: Someone who has taken a tumble is looking for a way to get moving again.
explanation.walkthrough: The fall is a fall of snow, not a tumble; SLEIGH and SLAY are said alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A sledge pulled over snow is how people travel once heavy snowfall has blocked ordinary transport.

clue.text: House lacks south wing? What a surprise!

indicators.note: lacking something means going without it, so one letter is taken away

parts.note: the House of Lords, the upper chamber of the UK Parliament
S is the compass abbreviation for south, here sitting at one side, or wing, of the word

explanation.surface: A building is missing its southern wing, to someone's astonishment.
explanation.walkthrough: The House is the House of Lords, Parliament's upper chamber; drop the S at the end of its name.
explanation.definitionFit: As an exclamation, invoking God by this title expresses shock or amazement, like 'Good heavens!'

clue.text: Cross Siberia travelling with Communist League vans

indicators.note: travelling letters move about, ending up in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the van is the front of a procession, so only the opening letters are used

parts.note: the first letter of each of these two words

explanation.surface: Someone crosses Siberia in vans belonging to a Communist League.
explanation.walkthrough: Cross looks like a verb about travelling across Siberia; it is the adjective meaning angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone quick-tempered and easily angered is irritable, and cross is the everyday word for annoyed.

clue.text: A way to interrupt female only set

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so a piece sits inside another

parts.note: a hen party or hen night is for women only
taken as written
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A route cuts into a women-only group.
explanation.walkthrough: A hen party is the British name for a women-only celebration before a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Concrete or jelly that sets becomes firm, so to set and to harden both mean to solidify.

clue.text: Advance to be doubled — you don't mean that, surely?

indicators.note: doubled tells us to write the word for advance twice, side by side

parts.note: to come is to advance or approach; written out twice as the clue asks

explanation.surface: A chess or board-game move is about to be doubled, and someone protests in disbelief.
explanation.definitionFit: The doubled exclamation is a spoken rebuke expressing disbelief or mild reproach at what another person has said.

clue.text: Point at which weight is concentrated = v

definitions.text: Point at which weight is concentrated
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the physics term for the balance point of a body
second meaning, read literally: v is the middle letter of the seven-letter word gravity

explanation.walkthrough: The equals sign makes it look like a physics formula with v for velocity; the answer read literally describes where v sits in gra-v-ity.
explanation.definitionFit: Physicists call the single point through which a body's whole mass effectively acts its balance point in this way.

clue.text: Moon shot? College is game!

indicators.note: something shot is wrecked or broken up, so the letters come apart and reform

parts.note: the four letters rearranged
a poly is a polytechnic, a kind of British college

explanation.surface: A college treats a moon landing as a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moon shot' reads as a space launch; shot is the signal to rearrange. A poly was a British polytechnic college.
explanation.definitionFit: The board game of buying property and charging rent is a famous family pastime.

clue.text: Sulphur extracted from beyond earth is rich

indicators.note: something extracted is pulled out, so that letter is removed from the word

parts.note: cosmic describes outer space, beyond the earth
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: Sulphur mined from beyond our planet would be a rich find.
explanation.walkthrough: Rich here is the informal sense, amusing or ridiculous, as in 'that's rich'.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling a remark rich means it is laughable or ironic, so it is funny in the way a humorous thing is.

clue.text: Factory in lane, possibly one of a modern generation

indicators.note: possibly tells us this is only one of the ways those letters could be arranged

parts.note: a mill is a factory
these six letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A factory set in a country lane might belong to a young entrepreneur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link placing the factory; it is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names a person born roughly between the early 1980s and late 1990s, the generation following Generation X.

clue.text: Dash on hearing 'rehearsal'

indicators.note: in this across clue on means placed after, so the dash comes second, behind the hearing

parts.note: a court hearing is a trial
to dash is to run

explanation.surface: Someone rushes off on being told of a rehearsal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dash on hearing' puts the dash after the hearing in the answer; hearing is a court case, not listening.
explanation.definitionFit: A practice attempt made before the real event is a test of the plan, just as a rehearsal is.

clue.text: That is awfully mean to put one out

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so the letters of mean come out in a jumbled order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: putting one out removes that piece from the word, leaving the rest

parts.note: to lay something is to put it down
a means one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: Someone protests that it is terribly unkind to exclude a person.
explanation.walkthrough: NAME comes from rearranging MEAN; then LAY loses its A to give LY. 'Put one out' looks like the definition of mean, but it is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Both introduce a specific clarification, the way the abbreviation i.e. or the word videlicet does.

clue.text: Bright-red tool on reversing crane

parts.note: cherry is a bright red colour
a pick is a digging tool

indicators.note: reversing means the short word for on is read backwards

parts.note: re means on or about, as in a memo

explanation.surface: A bright red tool is mounted on a crane that is backing up.
explanation.definitionFit: The vehicle carries a hydraulic lifting platform on an arm, a kind of small crane used for raising workers.

clue.text: Ballet etc fragments prior to change

indicators.note: to change is to alter, so the letters are rearranged into new words

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bits of ballet and the like before a costume change.
explanation.definitionFit: Dance, drama and music performed live before an audience are grouped together under this collective term.

clue.text: It indicates action of lover boy's heart

indicators.note: the heart of a phrase is its middle, so the answer sits concealed in the central letters

parts.note: the four letters at the centre of the two words run together

explanation.surface: Something reveals what a romantic young man's heart is doing.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, a doing word names an action or state, which is the part of speech the clue describes.

clue.text: One joining Plato in discursive medium

indicators.note: discursive means rambling from point to point, so the letters wander out of order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone joins Plato in a rambling philosophical discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medium' looks like a spiritualist next to Plato, but here it is an artist's material.
explanation.definitionFit: Artists call the substance they work in their medium, and pigment ground in linseed is a classic one.

clue.text: Gorilla at play, that has an enormous bite

indicators.note: things at play move about freely, so these letters tumble into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A playful gorilla delivers a fearsome bite.
explanation.definitionFit: The large reptile with powerful jaws is famous for one of the strongest bite forces in the animal kingdom.

clue.text: Success with female, initially triumphing only so far

parts.note: a hit is a success
her is the female pronoun

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the next words

parts.note: the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A woman's success so far has been a partial triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: The formal adverb means up to this point in time, just as the everyday phrase so far does.

clue.text: Cancelled electronic dial for the present

parts.note: a cancelled event is off
E is the standard abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail
to dial someone is to ring them

explanation.surface: An electronic dial has been switched off for now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For the present' looks like 'for now'; it is a link and the definition, a present meaning a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Something given as a gift or tribute is an offering, the same as a present handed over.

clue.text: Disclosure taken by peer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a release of secret information
second meaning: read peer as one who pees, and what such a person takes

explanation.surface: A revelation is picked up by a member of the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: Peer looks like a lord; split it as pee-er, someone who urinates, who in slang takes a leak.
explanation.definitionFit: An unauthorised release of information, and the slang phrase for urinating, both use this one short word.

clue.text: Caught on camera covered in PVC?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: wrapped in a thin plastic sheet such as cling wrap

explanation.surface: Someone dressed in PVC is spotted by a camera.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that PVC is only one example of a plastic layer.
explanation.definitionFit: Recorded with a movie camera, and coated with a thin plastic layer, are both senses of this past participle.

clue.text: Astounding, inspiring

definitions.meaning: first meaning: so impressive it leaves you speechless
second meaning, taken literally: drawing air into the lungs

explanation.walkthrough: Inspiring sounds like a second word for astounding, but it is meant literally: to inspire is to inhale.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes something amazing, and read literally it describes the act of drawing in air.

clue.text: Sound made by car (old)

parts.note: Audi is a German make of car
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A noise comes from an old car.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names recorded or transmitted sound, as opposed to the picture, in broadcasting.

clue.text: See 12
Modern means of hooking up — it should catch well

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a well-known dating app
second meaning: dry material that takes a spark readily

explanation.surface: A dating app ought to land you a good catch.
explanation.definitionFit: The phone app arranges casual dates, while dry kindling is used to light a fire because it ignites easily.

clue.text: Juvenile leads in iconic musical needing to grow up

indicators.note: the leads of words are their front letters, so we keep only the first of each

parts.note: the opening letter of each of these two words
to mature is to grow up

explanation.surface: A child star in a famous musical has to grow up.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone young and childish has not yet developed fully, which is what juvenile describes.

clue.text: Technological aspects of farming sparking angry mood almost

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of mood is dropped
sparking sets things off, so the letters fly into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
the word without its last letter

explanation.surface: The technical side of agriculture puts someone in a foul temper.
explanation.definitionFit: The science of soil management and crop production is the applied, technical side of agriculture.

clue.text: Force of habit, eating last of tiramisu

indicators.note: something eating takes another thing inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a habit is a garment, as worn by a nun

indicators.note: last of means we keep only the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the final letter of the dessert

explanation.surface: Someone eats tiramisu out of sheer habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force of habit' is a stock phrase; split it after force. A nun's habit is her dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Compulsion by threats or pressure, as in signing under duress, is coercion or force.
